reader.summary: The week was dominated by a surge in US-Russia diplomacy. US envoy Steve Witkoff traveled to St. Petersburg to meet President Putin, calling him a 'humanitarian' and pressing for an end to the war. The Kremlin responded by agreeing to three-way peace talks with Ukraine and the US in early November in Abu Dhabi. Melania Trump brokered a one-city humanitarian ceasefire in the Russian-occupied town of Oleshky, and Russia released 74-year-old American Stephen Hubbard after more than four years in a Russian jail. In a controversial move, Trump waived several newly enacted sanctions on Russian energy just before a new law took effect, angering Zelensky and parts of Congress. On the battlefield, Ukraine launched some of its largest drone attacks of the year, hitting Moscow-area airports, data centers, and Putin's hometown, while Russia pounded Kyiv with cluster bombs and missiles. The first tanker of Russian diesel under the Trump-Putin trade deal set sail for the US. Romania blamed Russia for a drone strike that sank a cargo ship in the Black Sea, killing one. Austria expel four Russian diplomats over espionage, and Germany arrested a Ukrainian man suspected of spying for Moscow. Russia's central bank held its key rate at 14 percent while raising its inflation forecast.

key_events.event: US envoy Steve Witkoff met Putin in St. Petersburg to discuss ending the Ukraine war and proposed a three-way summit with Trump and Xi.
Russia and Ukraine agreed to a one-city humanitarian ceasefire in the occupied town of Oleshky, brokered by Melania Trump.
Russia freed 74-year-old American Stephen Hubbard after more than four years in a Russian jail, at Trump's request.
Trump waived several newly enacted sanctions on Russian energy just before a new law took effect, drawing criticism from Zelensky and Congress.
Russia, Ukraine, and the US agreed to hold three-way peace talks in Abu Dhabi in early November.
Ukraine launched over 1,000 drones at Russia in one of its largest attacks of the year, hitting airports, data centers, and Putin's hometown.
The first tanker of Russian diesel under the Trump-Putin trade deal set sail for the US.
Romania blamed Russia for a drone strike that sank a cargo ship in the Black Sea, killing one and leaving three missing.
Austria expelled four Russian diplomats linked to espionage, and Germany arrested a Ukrainian man suspected of spying for Moscow.
Russia's central bank held its key rate at 14 percent while raising its 2026 inflation forecast amid war-driven price pressures.

crystal.summary: Next week, the diplomatic momentum from the Witkoff-Putin meeting will drive headlines as the US, Russia and Ukraine prepare for the early-November Abu Dhabi talks. A joint agenda or pre-talks working meeting will be the most concrete diplomatic step, settling whether the Trump-Xi-Putin summit will proceed in parallel. On the battlefield, Russia will test its newly built jet-powered drones in a strike on Ukrainian infrastructure, and the drone-and-missile exchange will intensify as both sides position for negotiations. In Washington, the Zelensky-Trump confrontation over the energy ceasefire will push Congress toward a formal challenge to the sanctions waiver, while the diesel tanker sails toward American ports. The Oleshky ceasefire will see its first aid convoys attempted, and the Black Sea ship sinking will linger as a diplomatic irritant.

display.headline: Russia Tests Jet Drones as Abu Dhabi Talks Take Shape
emoji_reasons: The Abu Dhabi peace talks and Oleshky ceasefire dominate the diplomatic landscape
Both sides will trade intensified drone and missile strikes on infrastructure
Congress will formally challenge the energy sanctions waiver
display.tldr: Next week centers on preparation for the early-November Abu Dhabi peace talks, with a joint agenda or pre-talks meeting as the key diplomatic milestone. Russia will test its new jet-powered drones in combat, and Congress will move to formally challenge the energy sanctions waiver.
display.eli5:
Right now, the US, Russia, and Ukraine are getting ready to sit down and talk in Abu Dhabi in early November. This week, an American envoy met Putin in St. Petersburg, and they agreed to hold these talks. Next week, the three sides will work out what exactly they will discuss, and there is a question about whether China's leader will also be at the table.

On the battlefield, both sides are hitting each other hard with drones and missiles. Russia just built a new base for fast jet-powered drones, and next week it will probably use them for the first time in a real attack on Ukrainian power plants or data centers. This is the jet-powered drone first combat use that forecasters are watching.

In Washington, Congress is angry that the president paused sanctions on Russian oil. Ukraine's leader is publicly arguing with the president about it. Next week, lawmakers will likely put a formal challenge on the table, forcing the White House to explain itself. This is the energy sanctions congressional challenge.

The big surprise would be if the cargo ship that sank in the Black Sea turns into a bigger diplomatic fight between Romania and Russia, making the peace talks harder to pull off.
